simple.meaning: הֶרֶג (hereg) is a Hebrew object word meaning “slaughter.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Esther 9:5. The surrounding context includes death, land, mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הֶרֶג (H2027) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

occurrences.englishText: The Jews struck all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, and with slaughter and destruction, and did what they wanted to those who hated them.
Rescue those who are being led away to death!
Has he struck them as he struck those who struck them? Or are they killed like those who killed them were killed?
There will be brooks and streams of water on every lofty mountain and on every high hill in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.
“The Lord Yahweh says to Tyre: ‘Won’t the islands shake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan, when the slaughter is made within you?
